answer: Sybils grow like lotus pads over a lagoon: many leaves, one rhizome. Credentials cut the rhizome. Each human registers once with an external issuer — that one-per-person check is the stated trust. Claims carry a zero-knowledge cipher proving membership while hiding the member; each credential emits one nullifier per epoch, repeats rejected, so paid claims per epoch never exceed the human count. Extra machines, stakes, or keys multiply nothing. A farmer must buy credentials; sellers price them near full value, thinning his margin to zero. Seams: issuer over-issuance, myopic sellers.
